title: Predicate-Initial Word Order and the 'Ay' Inversion
subtitle: Discover the natural predicate-first structure and formal inversion in Filipino
keyPoint: Natural conversational Filipino places the predicate before the subject, whereas using the particle 'ay' moves the subject to the beginning for formal or literary emphasis.

useCases.label: Everyday Conversation
useCases.example: Mabait ang doktor.

useCases.label: Formal Speeches or Writing
useCases.example: Ang doktor ay mabait.

useCases.label: Action Focus in Daily Talk
useCases.example: Nagluluto si Maria.

examples.en: Maganda ang umaga.
Masaya ang mga mag-aaral.
Nars ang kapatid ko.
Ang Pilipinas ay maganda.
Umiinom ng tubig ang lalaki.

mistakes.note: Filipino does not use English SVO without the particle 'ay'; you must lead with the predicate or insert 'ay'.
Do not insert 'ay' when the predicate already leads the sentence.
The particle 'ay' only links a fronted subject to its following predicate, never a fronted verb to its subject.

quiz.question: How do you naturally say 'The dog is big' in everyday spoken Filipino?
quiz.explanation: Conversational Filipino naturally follows Predicate (Malaki) + Subject (ang aso).

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly uses the formal inversion particle 'ay'?
quiz.explanation: 'Ay' is placed strictly between the fronted topic/subject and the predicate.

quiz.question: Complete the natural spoken sentence: '___ ang bahay.' (New is the house)
quiz.explanation: The predicate adjective 'Bago' belongs right at the start of a predicate-initial sentence.

quiz.question: Convert 'Masipag ang nanay' into the inverted 'ay' order:
quiz.explanation: The subject 'Ang nanay' moves to the front, followed by 'ay', followed by 'masipag'.

tip: Speak like a native by avoiding 'ay' in everyday conversation; start directly with the adjective, noun, or verb predicate.

title: Direct, Indirect, and Oblique Markers (Ang, Ng, Sa)
subtitle: Master the primary case-marking particles for common nouns in Filipino
keyPoint: 'Ang' marks the central topic/focus, 'ng' marks the direct object or possessor, and 'sa' marks location, direction, or recipient.

useCases.label: Topic Identification
useCases.example: Malamig ang tubig.

useCases.label: Possession and Objects
useCases.example: Binasa ko ang libro ng bata.

useCases.label: Location and Direction
useCases.example: Nasa mesa ang pagkain.

examples.en: Kumain ang pusa ng isda.
Nasa kusina ang nanay.
Ito ang susi ng bahay.
Naglakad ang mag-aaral sa paaralan.
Malinis ang mga silid.

mistakes.note: An actor-focus verb can only have one 'ang' phrase; the object takes 'ng'.
Destinations take the oblique marker 'sa', not 'ng'.
Possession is marked with 'ng' (e.g., 'bahay ng guro'), not 'sa'.

quiz.question: Select the correct marker for the object: 'Uminom ang lalaki ___ gatas.'
quiz.explanation: In an actor-focus sentence, the direct object is marked with 'ng'.

quiz.question: Select the marker indicating location: 'Nasa ___ mesa ang tasa.'
quiz.explanation: The location marker for common nouns is 'sa'.

quiz.question: Select the focused subject marker: 'Mabilis ___ kabayo.'
quiz.explanation: 'Ang' marks the grammatical subject/topic of the predicate 'mabilis'.

quiz.question: Select the marker showing possession: 'Ito ang kotse ___ doktor.'
quiz.explanation: 'Ng' marks the possessor ('of the doctor').

tip: Remember: 'ang' = the focus (like a spotlight), 'ng' = of / non-focus object, and 'sa' = to / in / on.

title: Personal Proper Noun Markers (Si, Ni, Kay)
subtitle: Mark personal names accurately across focus, genitive, and oblique cases
keyPoint: Use 'si', 'ni', and 'kay' exclusively before names of individuals instead of the common noun markers 'ang', 'ng', and 'sa'.

useCases.label: Person as Focus
useCases.example: Mabait si Pedro.

useCases.label: Possession by a Person
useCases.example: Kotse ito ni Pedro.

useCases.label: Direction / Recipient (Person)
useCases.example: Ibigay mo ito kay Pedro.

examples.en: Doktor si Rosa.
Gawa ito ni Carlo.
Pumunta kami kay Miguel.
Dumating sina nanay at tatay.
Sulat ito mula kina Ana.

mistakes.note: Use 'si' instead of 'ang' for personal names.
Use 'ni' instead of 'ng' when marking possession by a person.
Use 'kay' instead of 'sa' for personal recipient or destination.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'Nagluto ___ Nanay ng hapunan.'
quiz.explanation: 'Si' marks a single person's name or familial title as the topic.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'Ito ang bag ___ Elena.'
quiz.explanation: 'Ni' marks possession by a named person.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'Ipaabot mo ang ulam ___ Tatay.'
quiz.explanation: 'Kay' marks the personal recipient.

quiz.question: How do you mark two named subjects as focus: 'Aalis na ___ Marco at Luis.'?
quiz.explanation: 'Sina' is the plural nominative marker for personal names.

tip: Pair them in your head: 'ang = si', 'ng = ni', 'sa = kay'. If it's a person's name, switch to the rhyming personal set!

title: Three-Case Pronoun Sets (Ako, Ko, Akin)
subtitle: Choose the right pronoun set for focus, actor/possessor, and beneficiary
keyPoint: Filipino pronouns correspond to the three noun cases: Ang-set (topic), Ng-set (actor/possessor), and Sa-set (location/beneficiary/preposed possessor).

useCases.label: Topic / Subject Pronoun
useCases.example: Masaya ako ngayon.

useCases.label: Post-nominal Possessor
useCases.example: Ito ang bahay ko.

useCases.label: Pre-nominal Possessor / Beneficiary
useCases.example: Akin ang librong ito.

examples.en: Gusto ko ng mangga.
Mabait siya sa amin.
Kinuha mo ba ang payong?
Para sa kaniya ang bulaklak.
Nagsasalita kami ng Tagalog.

mistakes.note: Use the Ng-set pronoun 'ko' for possession, not the Ang-set 'ako'.
Pseudo-verbs like 'gusto' take the Ng-set pronoun ('ko') to express who desires the action.
After prepositions like 'para sa', use the Sa-set pronoun ('akin').

quiz.question: Choose the correct pronoun: 'Pumunta ___ sa palengke kahapon.' (I)
quiz.explanation: 'Ako' is the Ang-set pronoun used as the subject of an actor-focus verb.

quiz.question: Choose the correct pronoun: 'Kinain ___ ang saging.' (by you / you ate)
quiz.explanation: 'Mo' is the Ng-set pronoun marking the non-subject agent in object-focus sentences.

quiz.question: Choose the correct pronoun: 'Sa ___ ba ang kotseng ito?' (yours)
quiz.explanation: 'Iyo' is the Sa-set pronoun indicating ownership after 'sa'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct pronoun: 'Nagluto si nanay para sa ___.' (him/her)
quiz.explanation: 'Kaniya' is the Sa-set pronoun required after the prepositional marker 'sa'.

tip: Short Ng-set pronouns like 'ko' and 'mo' are enclitic: they never stand alone at the very beginning of a sentence and always attach tightly after the first word.

title: Existential and Possessive Markers (May, Mayroon, Wala)
subtitle: Express presence, possession, and absence with non-verbal predicates
keyPoint: Use 'may' directly before nouns/verbs without a linker, 'mayroon' when followed by enclitics or standing alone, and 'wala' to state absence or non-possession.

cells: There is food on the table.
Followed by monosyllabic pronoun or linker (-g/-ng)
Short affirmative answer ('Yes, there is / I have')
Negation of may/mayroon; requires linker before noun
There is no water in the glass.

useCases.label: Simple Existence / Presence
useCases.example: May tao sa loob.

useCases.label: Possession with Pronouns
useCases.example: Mayroon siyang bagong kotse.

useCases.label: Absence or Lack
useCases.example: Walang pasok ngayon.

examples.en: May pera ka ba?
Mayroon kaming bisita.
Walang problema dito.
May aso sa bakuran.
Wala akong pera ngayon.

mistakes.note: If an enclitic pronoun like 'ako' immediately follows the existential predicate, you must use 'mayroon', not 'may'.
Never attach enclitic particles or linkers directly onto 'may'; use 'mayroon' instead.
'Wala' must connect to the following noun or pronoun using the ligature -ng / na.

quiz.question: Complete the existential sentence: '___ pusa sa ilalim ng kama.' (There is a cat...)
quiz.explanation: 'May' is placed directly before a bare noun without any linker or enclitic pronoun intervening.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly expresses 'I have a question'?
quiz.explanation: When an enclitic pronoun ('ako') follows immediately, 'mayroon' must be used with the ligature ('akong').

quiz.question: Select the correct form to say 'There is no rice':
quiz.explanation: 'Wala' attaches the ligature '-ng' to the succeeding word: 'Walang kanin'.

quiz.question: How do you answer a simple yes/no existence question affirmatively ('Do you have coffee? - Yes, I have')?
quiz.explanation: 'Mayroon' can stand independently as a complete affirmative answer, while 'may' can never stand alone.

tip: Quick trick: 'May' is glued straight to the noun ('May libro'). If you need to slip in a pronoun first ('ako', 'ka', 'siya'), expand it to 'Mayroon' ('Mayroon akong libro').

title: Demonstrative Pronoun Systems
subtitle: Master spatial proximity with ito, iyan, and iyon across cases
keyPoint: Filipino demonstratives distinguish three distances (near speaker, near listener, far from both) across nominative, genitive, and locative cases.

useCases.label: Pointing to an object near you
useCases.example: Masarap ang manggang ito.

useCases.label: Indicating possession or source
useCases.example: Uminom siya ng tubig mula rito.

useCases.label: Specifying a distant location
useCases.example: Nakatira ang lola ko roon.

examples.en: Ano ang ibig sabihin nito?
Gusto ko ang sapatos na ito.
Pumunta ka roon sa tindahan.
Hawakan mo iyan nang maayos.
Maganda ang tanawin doon.

mistakes.right: Gusto ko ang mansanas na ito.
mistakes.note: Demonstratives acting as adjectives require the linker na/-ng after the noun.
Use 'nandito' or simply 'dito' rather than combining 'nasa' with 'dito'.

mistakes.wrong: Kumain ako niyan kanina sa bahay ko.
mistakes.right: Kumain ako nito kanina sa bahay ko.
mistakes.note: Use 'nito' for things close to the speaker, not 'niyan' which points near the listener.

quiz.question: What is the correct nominative demonstrative for something close to the listener? '___ ang payong mo.'
quiz.explanation: 'Iyan' refers to objects near the person being addressed.

quiz.question: Choose the genitive pronoun for an object held by the speaker: 'Uminom ka ___.'
quiz.explanation: 'Nito' is the genitive/object marker for things proximate to the speaker.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank for a location far from both speaker and listener: 'Magkita tayo ___ bukas.'
quiz.explanation: 'Doon' indicates a location distant from both interlocutors.

quiz.question: Identify the locative form for a place right next to the listener: 'Ilagay mo ang bag ___.'
quiz.explanation: 'Diyan' indicates proximity to the listener.

tip: Locative forms change their initial 'd' to 'r' (dito -> rito, doon -> roon) when the preceding word ends in a vowel.

title: Actor Focus Verbs: -Um- vs. Mag-
subtitle: Distinguish internal actions from deliberate, external activities
keyPoint: The infix -um- typically marks internal, reflexive, or natural movements, whereas the prefix mag- indicates deliberate, repetitive, or transitive actions.

useCases.label: Expressing natural physical acts
useCases.example: Uminom siya ng malamig na tubig.

useCases.label: Executing deliberate occupational tasks
useCases.example: Nagtatrabaho ang kuya ko sa ospital.

useCases.label: Pairing reciprocal or outward motions
useCases.example: Naglalaro ang mga bata sa labas.

examples.en: Pumunta kami sa Maynila kahapon.
Nagsipilyo siya bago matulog.
Umulan nang malakas kagabi.
Mag-aaral ako ng Filipino mamaya.
Bumangon ang bata nang maaga.

mistakes.note: Weather occurrences and natural phenomena take -um-, never mag-.
'Kain' takes the -um- affix (kumain) for personal consumption, not mag-.

mistakes.wrong: Umaral ako kagabi para sa pagsusulit.
mistakes.right: Nag-aral ako kagabi para sa pagsusulit.
mistakes.note: 'Aral' takes mag- (nag-aral) when meaning studying intensely.

quiz.question: Choose the correct verb for drinking water: 'Mabilis siyang ___ ng gatas.'
quiz.explanation: 'Inom' standardly forms an actor-focus verb with -um- (uminom).

quiz.question: Which verb correctly expresses deliberate cooking? 'Si Nanay ay ___ ng adobo.'
quiz.explanation: 'Luto' takes mag- in actor focus; the imperfective form is 'nagluluto'.

quiz.question: Select the correct form for weather: 'Biglang ___ ang hangin kanina.'
quiz.explanation: Natural shifts in state or weather use -um- (lumakas).

quiz.question: Fill in the blank with the appropriate verb for cleaning: '___ ako ng maruming kuwarto.'
quiz.explanation: 'Linis' in actor focus commonly takes mag- (naglinis in past/completed aspect).

tip: If a root begins with a vowel, prefix 'um-' directly (e.g., umalis); if it begins with a consonant, insert '-um-' after the first consonant (e.g., s-um-ulat).

title: Aspectual Conjugation
subtitle: Master Contemplated, Imperfective, and Perfective aspects
keyPoint: Filipino verbs mark aspect (completion of action) rather than tense, utilizing first-syllable reduplication and affix shifts.

useCases.label: Describing finished actions (Perfective)
useCases.example: Kumanta ang mang-aawit sa entablado.

useCases.label: Describing ongoing or habitual actions (Imperfective)
useCases.example: Kumakanta siya tuwing umaga.

useCases.label: Describing future or intended actions (Contemplated)
useCases.example: Kakanta kami sa pista bukas.

examples.en: Bumabasa siya ng bagong aklat ngayon.
Tatakbo ako sa parke bukas ng madaling-araw.
Tumawag ang doktor kaninang tanghali.
Nagsasalita ang guro sa harap ng klase.
Magluluto si Tatay ng hapunan mamaya.

mistakes.wrong: Sumulat ako bukas sa aking kaibigan.
mistakes.right: Susulat ako bukas sa aking kaibigan.
mistakes.note: The contemplated aspect drops the -um- infix and only reduplicates the first CV syllable (susulat).

mistakes.wrong: Kahapon ay kakain siya sa restawran.
mistakes.right: Kahapon ay kumain siya sa restawran.
mistakes.note: 'Kakain' is contemplated (future); use the perfective 'kumain' for actions completed yesterday.

mistakes.wrong: Kasalukuyang nagluto ang ate ko ngayon.
mistakes.right: Kasalukuyang nagluluto ang ate ko ngayon.
mistakes.note: Ongoing actions require the imperfective form with reduplication (nagluluto).

quiz.question: Identify the contemplated (unstarted) aspect of 'alis': '___ kami mamayang gabi.'
quiz.explanation: Contemplated aspect duplicates the first syllable: a- + alis = 'aalis'.

quiz.question: Which verb form denotes an ongoing action right now? 'Si Pedro ay ___ sa telepono.'
quiz.explanation: 'Tumatawag' uses the -um- infix with first-syllable reduplication for progressive/habitual aspect.

quiz.question: Choose the perfective (completed) aspect for 'tulong': '___ sila sa aming proyekto kahapon.'
quiz.explanation: 'Tumulong' represents completed action without syllable reduplication.

quiz.question: What is the imperfective form of the mag- verb 'aral'? 'Siya ay palaging ___ gabi-gabi.'
quiz.explanation: Mag- verbs become nag- + CV reduplication (nag-aaral) in the imperfective aspect.

tip: Reduplication in Filipino always copies just the initial consonant and vowel (CV) of the root, never consonant clusters (e.g., 'prito' becomes 'piprito').

title: Patient/Object Focus with -In Verbs
subtitle: Promote the direct recipient of an action to the ang-trigger role
keyPoint: In object-focus sentences, the suffix -in/-hin targets the patient as the subject (marked by ang), while the agent takes the genitive marker (ng).

useCases.label: Emphasizing a specific object acted upon
useCases.example: Ininom ng bata ang sariwang gatas.

useCases.label: Issuing direct patient-oriented commands
useCases.example: Basahin mo ang maikling kuwento.

useCases.label: Describing habitual object-focused actions
useCases.example: Lulutuin ni Nanay ang paborito mong ulam.

examples.en: Kinain ng pusa ang isda sa mesa.
Tawagin mo ang iyong kapatid ngayon.
Binabasa ni Maria ang makapal na libro.
Gagawin ko ang aking takdang-aralin mamaya.
Linisin natin ang buong bahay bukas.

mistakes.note: In patient focus, the actor must take the genitive pronoun (ko), not the nominative (ako).
The patient of an object-focus verb must be flagged with the trigger marker 'ang', not 'ng'.
In the completed aspect, the suffix -in drops when the infix -in- is added.

quiz.question: Identify the correct actor pronoun: 'Gagawin ___ ang proyekto bukas.'
quiz.explanation: Patient-focus verbs require the actor to be in the genitive case ('ko').

quiz.question: Select the correct contemplated form of 'bili': '___ ni Juan ang bagong kotse sa susunod na taon.'
quiz.explanation: 'Bili' takes -hin with reduplication to form 'bibilhin' in the contemplated aspect.

quiz.question: What is the perfective form of 'luto' in patient focus? '___ ni Nanay ang masarap na sinigang.'
quiz.explanation: Roots starting with /l/ undergo metathesis: 'linuto' regularly becomes 'niluto'.

quiz.question: Complete the command: '___ mo ang gamot pagkatapos kumain.'
quiz.explanation: Direct object-focused commands use the infinitive suffix form: root 'inom' + '-in' = 'inumin'.

tip: When a root ends in an open vowel without a glottal stop, use the suffix '-hin' instead of '-in' (e.g., basa -> basahin).

title: The Ligature (Na / -ng)
subtitle: Connect modifiers, adjectives, and clauses smoothly
keyPoint: The ligature links modifiers to their head words using '-ng' attached after vowels or 'n', and the standalone word 'na' following consonants.

useCases.label: Linking adjectives to nouns
useCases.example: Bumili siya ng matamis na mangga.

useCases.label: Linking numbers or quantifiers to nouns
useCases.example: May tatlong pusa sa ilalim ng mesa.

useCases.label: Embedding subordinate or relative clauses
useCases.example: Ito ang bahay na itinayo ng aking ama.

examples.en: Malamig na tubig ang gusto kong inumin.
May limang aklat sa ibabaw ng lamesa.
Mabait na bata ang anak ni Teresa.
Pumasok ang bagong guro sa aming silid.
Masarap na pagkain ang inihanda nila.

mistakes.note: Modifiers cannot directly precede nouns without a ligature (-ng/na).
Since 'matalino' ends in a vowel (o), you must attach '-ng' directly rather than using separate 'na'.

mistakes.right: Malamig na tubig ang ininom ko.
mistakes.note: Because 'malamig' ends in a consonant (g), the standalone particle 'na' is mandatory.

quiz.question: Connect 'mainit' (hot) to 'kape' (coffee): 'Gusto ko ng ___ kape.'
quiz.explanation: 'Mainit' ends in the consonant 't', which requires the separate ligature particle 'na'.

quiz.question: Connect 'lima' (five) to 'tao' (people): 'May ___ pumunta sa handaan.'
quiz.explanation: 'Lima' ends in a vowel, so '-ng' attaches directly to the word: 'limang'.

quiz.question: What is the correct form for 'ulan' (rain/rainy) + ligature connecting to 'panahon' (season)?
quiz.explanation: Words ending in 'n' drop the final 'n' and add '-ng' (ulan -> ulang) or assimilate directly.

quiz.question: Choose the correct sentence featuring proper ligature usage:
quiz.explanation: 'Masarap' ends in a consonant, correctly taking the separate linker 'na' before 'prutas'.

tip: Filipino ligatures are bidirectional: 'mabuting tao' and 'taong mabuti' mean the exact same thing.

title: Split Negation System (Hindi, Huwag, Wala)
subtitle: Master the three core negative particles of Filipino
keyPoint: Filipino uses three distinct negative words depending on whether you are negating predicates (hindi), issuing prohibitions (huwag), or expressing non-existence and lack of possession (wala).

cells: Negates adjectives, nouns, and indicative verbs

useCases.label: Denying Facts or Predicates
useCases.example: Hindi ako pupunta sa opisina bukas.

useCases.label: Issuing Prohibitions
useCases.example: Huwag mong hawakan ang baso.

useCases.label: Asserting Absence or Non-possession
useCases.example: Wala siyang dalang payong.

examples.en: Hindi siya kumain ng tanghalian kanina.
Huwag kayong maingay sa loob ng silid-aklatan.
Wala nang kape sa tasa.
Hindi totoo ang balitang narinig mo.
Huwag kang matakot sumubok muli.

mistakes.note: Use 'huwag' instead of 'hindi' when commanding someone not to do something.
Possession and presence are negated using 'wala' rather than 'hindi'.
Adjectives and descriptive predicates must be negated with 'hindi', not 'wala'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct negative word: '___ kang mag-alala tungkol sa pagsusulit.' (Don't worry about the exam.)
quiz.explanation: 'Huwag' is required for negative imperatives (prohibitions).

quiz.question: Choose the correct negative word: '___ pa dumadating ang guro.' (The teacher hasn't arrived yet.)
quiz.explanation: Verbal predicates expressing facts are negated using 'hindi'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct negative word: '___ tao sa loob ng bahay.' (There is no one inside the house.)
quiz.explanation: Absence or lack of existence requires 'wala' (here combined with the ligature -ng: 'walang').

quiz.question: Choose the correct negative word: '___ asukal sa kusina.' (There is no sugar in the kitchen.)
quiz.explanation: 'Walang' (wala + -ng) is used to express the absence of a noun.

tip: Remember: 'Hindi' says it isn't so, 'Huwag' says don't do it, and 'Wala' says there isn't any!

title: Enclitic Particles (Ba, Na, Pa, Din/Rin, Naman, Kasi)
subtitle: Master second-position enclitics to sound natural
keyPoint: Enclitic particles cannot begin a sentence and must cling to the very first stressed word of the clause in a fixed order.

cells: It is your turn to read.

useCases.label: Asking Clarifying Questions
useCases.example: Nandito na ba ang sundo mo?

useCases.label: Expressing Completion vs. Continuance
useCases.example: Natutulog pa ang sanggol kanina.

useCases.label: Polite Turn-taking or Contrast
useCases.example: Ako naman ang susubok ngayon.

examples.en: Gusto mo ba ng malamig na tubig?
Tapos na ang klase namin kanina.
Nagluluto pa si Nanay ng hapunan.
Sasama rin ba ang kapatid mo?
Bakit kasi hindi ka nagtanong agad?

mistakes.note: Enclitic particles like 'ba' can never appear at the very beginning of a sentence.
The particle 'na' must precede 'din/rin' when multiple enclitics cluster together.
Use 'raw/rin' instead of 'daw/din' when following a word that ends in a vowel or semivowel (w, y).

quiz.question: Select the natural word order: 'Are you still studying?'
quiz.explanation: Monosyllabic pronoun 'ka' precedes enclitics 'pa' and 'ba' right after the initial verb.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank for 'already': 'Umalis ___ ang tren papuntang probinsya.'
quiz.explanation: 'Na' indicates an action that has already taken place.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly places 'din' (also) after a consonant?
quiz.explanation: After consonant endings (except w and y), use 'din' rather than 'rin'.

quiz.question: Select the correct particle indicating cause or explanation ('because'): 'Huli na ako ___ nasiraan ang bus.'
quiz.explanation: 'Kasi' indicates cause, reason, or mild justification.

tip: Short one-syllable personal pronouns like 'ka' jump ahead of enclitic particles, while longer pronouns come after them!

title: Directional and Benefactive Focus (I- and -An)
subtitle: Promote destinations, locations, and beneficiaries to the subject
keyPoint: The prefix i- typically focuses on the beneficiary for whom an action is performed, while the suffix -an focuses on the location, direction, or recipient of the action.

useCases.label: Doing an Action for Someone
useCases.example: Ibili mo ng bagong damit si Bunso.

useCases.label: Targeting a Specific Place
useCases.example: Pinuntahan ng mga turista ang magandang talon.

useCases.label: Performing an Action onto an Object
useCases.example: Punasan mo ang maruming mesa.

examples.en: Ibinili ni Pedro ng bulaklak ang kaniyang kasintahan.
Hinigupan niya ng mainit na sabaw ang mangkok.
Ipanghiram mo ng aklat ang kapatid mo sa silid-aklatan.
Tinakpan ng nanay ang ulam sa lamesa.
Igawa mo ng saranggola ang pamangkin mo.

mistakes.wrong: Bumili ako para sa kaniya ng prutas. (benefactive trigger)
mistakes.note: Filipino naturally promotes the beneficiary to the trigger using 'i-' rather than relying on periphrastic 'para sa'.
In locative focus (-an), the location takes the trigger article 'ang', not the directional preposition 'sa'.
Opening a door targets a surface/location of action, requiring suffix '-an' (buksan), not prefix 'i-'.

quiz.question: Choose the benefactive verb: '___ mo ng kape si Tatay.' (Make some coffee for Dad.)
quiz.explanation: 'Ipagtimpla' (i- + pag-) places the beneficiary 'si Tatay' as the syntactic trigger.

quiz.question: Choose the locative verb: '___ ng pintor ang lumang dingding.' (The painter painted on the old wall.)
quiz.explanation: The suffix '-an' (in completed aspect 'pininturahan') focuses on the surface or location being painted.

quiz.question: Complete the benefactive sentence: '___ ko ng pasalubong ang aking kapatid.' (I bought souvenirs for my sibling.)
quiz.explanation: 'Ibinili' uses benefactive focus to elevate the recipient sibling to the 'ang' phrase.

quiz.question: What is the trigger role in: 'Hinugasan ni Ana ang plato'?
quiz.explanation: The suffix '-an' in 'hinugasan' makes the plate ('ang plato') the locative/patient focus target.

tip: Think of 'i-' as offering something out toward someone (beneficiary), and '-an' as applying an action onto a surface or spot (location)!

title: Abilitative and Involuntary Moods (Maka- vs. Ma-)
subtitle: Distinguish deliberate actions from potential or accidental outcomes
keyPoint: Prefixes maka- (Actor Focus) and ma- (Patient Focus) convey either the ability to perform an act or that an event occurred accidentally and without deliberate intention.

cells: Nabasag ko ang baso nang hindi sinasadya.

useCases.label: Expressing Accidental Actions
useCases.example: Naiwan ko ang pitaka ko sa sasakyan.

useCases.label: Claiming Capability or Potential
useCases.example: Makakatapos din tayo ng pag-aaral sa wakas.

useCases.label: Perceptions Beyond Direct Will
useCases.example: Naamoy mo ba ang mabangong sampaguita?

examples.en: Hindi ako nakatulog kagabi dahil sa ingay.
Nabasag ang mamahaling plorera kanina.
Makakapunta ka ba sa kasal sa Sabado?
Nakalimutan kong dalhin ang libro mo.
Nauunawaan mo ba ang sinabi ng guro?

mistakes.wrong: Sinira ko ang salamin kahapon nang aksidente.
mistakes.right: Nasira ko ang salamin kahapon nang aksidente.
mistakes.note: Use 'na-' instead of deliberate focus '-in-' when an action is accidental or unintentional.

mistakes.wrong: Pumunta ako sa pulong kahapon dahil may lagnat ako.
mistakes.right: Hindi ako nakapunta sa pulong kahapon dahil may lagnat ako.
mistakes.note: Use 'naka-' or 'nakapag-' to express being able (or unable) to attend an event.
Abilitative future tense requires reduplication of the first syllable of the root: maka-ka-nood.

quiz.question: Choose the verb meaning 'accidentally dropped': '___ niya ang telepono sa sahig kanina.'
quiz.explanation: 'Nalaglag' expresses an involuntary or accidental dropping of something.

quiz.question: Choose the verb meaning 'can speak': '___ ka ba ng wikang Tagalog?'
quiz.explanation: 'Makapagsalita' denotes the physical or acquired ability to speak.

quiz.question: What does 'Nabasag ko ang baso' specifically imply compared to 'Binasag ko ang baso'?
options: The speaker did not break it.
quiz.explanation: The prefix 'na-' signals involuntary/accidental mood, meaning you broke it by accident.

quiz.question: Complete the potential ability sentence: 'Hindi siya ___ lumangoy sa malalim na dagat.' (He cannot swim in deep seas.)
quiz.explanation: 'Makalangoy' expresses the ability to swim.

tip: Whenever you did something by accident, apologize using 'na-' verbs (e.g., 'Nasagi kita!' instead of 'Sinagi kita!'), so people know you didn't do it intentionally!

title: Pseudo-Verbal Modal Constructions (Gusto, Nais, Ayaw, Dapat, Kailangan)
subtitle: Form compound clauses expressing desires, obligations, and necessities
keyPoint: Pseudo-verbs like gusto, ayaw, kailangan, and dapat act as modal predicates that link to complementary verbs using the ligature (-ng / na) and take either genitive or nominative actors depending on clause structure.

useCases.label: Expressing Desires and Preferences
useCases.example: Gusto kong maglakbay sa iba't ibang bansa.

useCases.label: Expressing Refusal or Aversion
useCases.example: Ayaw niyang kumain ng gulay.

useCases.label: Stating Obligations and Necessity
useCases.example: Dapat tayong rumespeto sa kapwa tao.

examples.en: Gusto kong matutong magsalita ng Filipino.
Ayaw nilang maghintay nang matagal sa pila.
Kailangan mong magsumite ng takdang-aralin ngayon.
Dapat tayong magtulungan upang matapos ang gawain.
Nais ng pangulo na magpatayo ng mga bagong paaralan.

mistakes.note: 'Gusto' requires a genitive actor pronoun ('ko') and the linker '-ng', not the nominative pronoun 'ako'.
Always attach the linker (-ng) to the pronoun preceding the complement verb.
The personal actor pronoun after 'ayaw' must bind to the infinitive via the ligature '-ng'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct pronoun and ligature: 'Gusto ___ magpahinga sa bahay.' (I want to rest at home.)
quiz.explanation: Gusto takes genitive actor 'ko' combined with the ligature '-ng' before the verb.

quiz.question: Complete the obligation: 'Dapat ___ sumunod sa batas trapiko.' (We [inclusive] should obey traffic laws.)
quiz.explanation: With 'dapat', the nominative pronoun 'tayo' with ligature '-ng' is standard: 'tayong sumunod'.

quiz.question: Choose the modal for refusal: '___ uminom ng gamot ang bata dahil mapait.' (The child refuses to take medicine because it's bitter.)
quiz.explanation: 'Ayaw' means to dislike, reject, or refuse to do an action.

quiz.question: Select the proper form of necessity: 'Kailangan ___ magmadali dahil mahuhuli na tayo.' (You need to hurry because we will be late.)
quiz.explanation: 'Kailangan' takes the genitive pronoun 'mo' plus the ligature '-ng' ('mong') before the complement verb.

tip: Always check for the ligature! Whether it is 'Gusto kong...', 'Dapat kang...', or 'Kailangan nating...', pseudo-verbs almost always demand a bridge particle (-ng / na) into the main action!

title: Reduplicative Morphology for Plurality and Intensity
subtitle: Repeat roots and syllables to show moderation, intensification, or distribution
keyPoint: Reduplicating root words with a linker denotes moderation or pretense, while doubling adjectives or roots expresses plural agreement or heightened intensity.

useCases.label: Plural Adjective Agreement
useCases.example: Magaganda ang mga tanawin sa probinsya.

useCases.label: Diminutive or Leisurely Action
useCases.example: Nagbasa-basa muna siya habang naghihintay.

useCases.label: Imitation or Pretend State
useCases.example: Naglalaro ang mga bata ng lutu-lutuan.

examples.en: Magagaling ang mga mang-aawit kagabi.
Umiinog-inog ang maliit na trumpo.
Tawa nang tawa ang mga manonood sa sinehan.
Nagsakit-sakitan ang bata para hindi pumasok sa klase.
Bumili sila ng sari-saring prutas sa palengke.

mistakes.note: Do not reduplicate the adjective when modifying a singular noun.
For continuous or frequentative repetitive action with 'nang', use the bare root before and after, not full inflected verbs.

mistakes.wrong: Kumakain-kain siya sa pormal na hapunan.
mistakes.right: Kumakain siya sa pormal na hapunan.
mistakes.note: Reduplicating the verb root implies casual, distracted, or snacking actions, which contradicts a formal dinner context.

quiz.question: Choose the correct plural form: 'The students are all smart.' -> '___ ang mga estudyante.'
quiz.explanation: Plural adjectives formed with 'ma-' reduplicate the first consonant-vowel syllable of the root (ta -> matatalino).

quiz.question: Which verb means 'to browse or read casually without deep concentration'?
quiz.explanation: Reduplicating the root ('basa-basa') creates a diminutive or moderative action indicating casual or leisurely activity.

quiz.question: Identify the expression meaning 'playing doctor' or 'make-believe doctor':
quiz.explanation: Adding reduplication plus the suffix '-an' (doktor-doktoran) denotes imitation, make-believe, or pretend play.

quiz.question: Which sentence indicates unceasing, repetitive crying?
quiz.explanation: 'Root + nang + root' (Iyak nang iyak) expresses an intense, relentless, and repetitive occurrence of the action.

tip: To describe an activity done aimlessly or to pass the time, simply reduplicate the verb's root after its normal aspect prefix (e.g., nag-isip-isip = pondered lightly).

title: Honorific Syntax and Formality Markers
subtitle: Positioning respect markers and honorific plural pronouns correctly in enclitic chains
keyPoint: The honorific particles 'po' and 'ho' occupy a specific slot within post-verbal enclitic clusters, immediately following monosyllabic pronouns but preceding multisyllabic pronouns.

cells: Kayo po ba si Dr. Reyes?

useCases.label: Affirmative Deference
useCases.example: Opo, natanggap ko na po ang liham.

useCases.label: Polite Inquiry to a Single Elder
useCases.example: Ano po ang maitutulong ko sa inyo?

useCases.label: Clitic Ordering with Monosyllables
useCases.example: Hindi ko na po alam ang sagot.

examples.en: Magandang umaga po sa inyong lahat.
Nais ko po sanang magtanong ukol sa proyekto.
Saan po kayo pupunta bukas?
Opo, darating na ho sila mamaya.
Huwag na po ninyong intindihin iyon.

mistakes.note: Use 'opo' exclusively as a standalone 'yes'; use 'po' inside sentences and greetings.
Monosyllabic clitic pronouns like 'mo' and 'ko' must precede 'po'.
When using 'po', shift second-person pronouns to the plural ('kayo', 'ninyo', 'inyo') even for a single listener.

quiz.question: Complete politely: 'Bakit ___ tinawag?'
quiz.explanation: Monosyllabic pronouns like 'mo' come before 'po', which comes before disyllabic pronouns like 'ako'.

quiz.question: Which response is the correct polite 'Yes' to an elder?
quiz.explanation: 'Opo' is the standard polite affirmative particle for 'yes'.

quiz.question: Select the properly ordered enclitic string: 'Hindi ___ nakita.'
quiz.explanation: Order: monosyllabic pronoun ('ko') + monosyllabic particle ('pa') + politeness marker ('po') + disyllabic pronoun ('siya').

quiz.question: How should you politely ask a single senior manager 'Where are you going?'
quiz.explanation: 'Kayo' replaces 'ka' for singular polite address, and 'po' precedes disyllabic 'kayo'.

tip: Remember the 1-syllable rule: monosyllabic clitics like 'ko', 'mo', 'na', and 'pa' always jump in front of 'po' (e.g., 'na po', 'ko po').

title: Causative Verbal Affixes
subtitle: Expressing induced, commanded, or permitted actions via Magpa- and Pa-...-in
keyPoint: Causative affixes insert an instigator who directs or allows an intermediary agent to execute an action upon a patient.

cells: Causer orders or permits someone to act
Induces someone to do an intransitive/transitive base
Object ordered to undergo an action
Causes intermediary to perform a mag- verb

useCases.label: Causer as Grammatical Subject
useCases.example: Nagpagawa si Maria ng bagong mesa sa karpintero.

useCases.label: Directing an Agent to Act
useCases.example: Pinakain ng nars ang pasyente ng gamot.

useCases.label: Focusing the Patient to Be Handled
useCases.example: Ipapadala ko ang dokumento sa koreo mamaya.

examples.en: Nagpagupit siya ng buhok sa bagong barbero.
Pinatulog ng ina ang sanggol sa duyan.
Huwag mong papasukin ang mga aso sa sala.
Ipagawa mo kay Pedro ang sirang pinto.
Papaglinisin ng guro ang mga estudyante ng silid-aralan.

mistakes.wrong: Naggupit siya ng buhok kahapon sa salon.
mistakes.right: Nagpagupit siya ng buhok kahapon sa salon.
mistakes.note: Use causative 'magpa-' when having a service done by someone else; 'naggupit' means you held the scissors yourself.

mistakes.wrong: Pinakain ko ang mangga sa bata.
mistakes.right: Ipinakain ko ang mangga sa bata.
mistakes.note: When the edible item (mangga) is the focus, use 'i- / ipa-', not patient focus 'pa-...-in' which triggers the eater.
In 'magpa-' actor-focus clauses, the causer takes 'ang' and the caused action's object takes 'ng'.

quiz.question: Which verb means 'to order/have someone clean the car' focusing on the owner who orders it?
quiz.explanation: 'Magpalinis' focuses on the causer who commissions the cleaning.

quiz.question: Choose the verb form focusing on the child sent home: '___ mo na ang bata.'
quiz.explanation: 'Pa-...-in' promotes the intermediary actor (the child who is ordered to go home) to focus.

quiz.question: How do you focus the car that needs repair: '___ ko ang kotse sa mekaniko.'
quiz.explanation: 'Ipapaayos' puts the patient/object being acted upon (ang kotse) into primary focus.

quiz.question: Which prefix is used to command someone to perform a 'mag-' verb (like mag-aral)?
quiz.explanation: 'Papag-...-in' is the causative affix reserved specifically for verbs whose base takes 'mag-'.

tip: Distinguish between 'pinakain' (fed someone = person is focus) and 'ipinakain' (fed something to someone = food is focus).

title: Instrumental Focus (I- / Ipang-)
subtitle: Elevating tools, instruments, and abstract reasons into the core subject trigger
keyPoint: Instrumental focus affixes 'i-' and 'ipang-' elevate the utensil, tool, or cause used to execute an action into the 'ang'-phrase.

useCases.label: Physical Tool Promotion
useCases.example: Ang kutsilyo ang ipinanghiwa niya sa karne.

useCases.label: Financial Resource as Means
useCases.example: Ipinambayad niya sa matrikula ang kanyang ipon.

useCases.label: Abstract Reason or Motivation
useCases.example: Ang kaligtasan ng pamilya ang ikinilos niya nang ganoon.

examples.en: Ipinangsulat niya ang lumang pluma sa liham.
Ano ang ipambubukas mo sa de-lata?
Ang bolpen na ito ang ipinangpirma ng pangulo sa kasunduan.
Ipinampunas ng weytres ang tuyong basahan sa maruming mesa.
Huwag mong ipanghiwa ng karne ang mapurol na kutsilyo.

mistakes.wrong: Hinugasan ko ang pinggan gamit ang espongha.
mistakes.right: Ipinanghugas ko sa pinggan ang espongha.
mistakes.note: While 'gamit ang' is spoken colloquial shorthand, idiomatic Filipino promotes the instrument directly using 'ipinang-'.
The instrument marked by 'ang' must be the tool used (bolpen), not the surface written upon (papel, which takes 'sa' or locative focus).

mistakes.wrong: Ipinaglinis niya ang walis sa sahig.
mistakes.right: Ipinanglinis niya ang walis sa sahig.
mistakes.note: 'Ipag-' is benefactive focus (for someone), whereas 'ipang-' is instrumental focus (using an object).

quiz.question: Identify the sentence where the instrument is the focus trigger:
options: Pumutol siya ng kahoy gamit ang palakol.
Pinutol niya ang kahoy sa gubat.
Ipinamputol niya ng kahoy ang palakol.
quiz.explanation: 'Ipinamputol' triggers 'ang palakol' (the ax) as the grammatical instrument subject.

quiz.question: What is the future instrumental form of 'bili' (nasal assimilation /b/ -> /m/)?
quiz.explanation: Before labial consonants /p/ and /b/, 'ipang-' assimilates to 'ipam-' followed by reduplication: 'ipambibili'.

quiz.question: Which affix expresses Benefactive focus (doing for someone) instead of Instrumental (using a tool)?
quiz.explanation: 'Ipag-' focuses on the beneficiary/benefactor, whereas 'ipang-' focuses on the instrument/tool.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence with the correct instrument trigger: 'Ipinansungkit niya ng mangga ang ___.'
quiz.explanation: The instrumental verb 'ipinansungkit' requires the tool used (ang mahabang kawayan) to be the focus.

tip: Watch nasal assimilation rules with 'ipang-': it becomes 'ipam-' before p/b (ipambura) and 'ipan-' before d/l/r/s/t (ipantali).

title: Sociative and Reciprocal Affixes
subtitle: Joining collective undertakings, requesting favors, and mutual interactions
keyPoint: Prefixes 'maki-' and 'makipag-' indicate participation in collective activities or requests for cooperation, while 'mag-...-an' captures mutual reciprocal actions.

cells: Joining an ongoing event / asking a favor
Initiating reciprocal interaction with another party
Dual or plural actors acting upon one another

useCases.label: Reciprocal Mutual Engagement
useCases.example: Nagyakapan ang magkaibigan matapos ang matagal na pagkawalay.

useCases.label: Joining a Group Activity
useCases.example: Nakisalo siya sa hapag-kainan ng pamilya.

useCases.label: Polite Formulaic Requests
useCases.example: Makisuyo nga po ng basong iyan sa mesa.

examples.en: Nakipagkasundo ang unyon sa pamunuan ng kumpanya.
Makikipagkita ako sa abogado bukas ng hapon.
Nagsisihan ang dalawang drayber sa banggaan.
Gusto kong makilaro sa inyong koponan.
Naghalikan ang mag-asawa pagkatapos ng seremonya.

mistakes.note: Reciprocal conversation between two parties requires 'nag-...-an' (nag-usapan) or reciprocal 'nag-usap' with hyphens before vowels.
When entering into a coordinated reciprocal activity with another entity introduced by 'kay/sa', use 'makipag-'.
To denote fighting each other mutually, the reciprocal suffix combination 'mag-...-an' (nagsuntukan) is mandatory.

quiz.question: Which verb means 'to talk with / engage in conversation with someone'?
quiz.explanation: 'Makipag-usap' indicates reaching out or engaging in reciprocal dialogue with a counterpart.

quiz.question: Choose the reciprocal form: 'The siblings helped each other.' -> 'Ang magkapatid ay ___.'
quiz.explanation: 'Mag-...-an' ('nagtulungan' in completed aspect) signifies symmetrical mutual action among group members.

quiz.question: What is the polite formula to ask to pass through a crowded doorway?
quiz.explanation: 'Makikiraan po' uses the sociative polite prefix 'maki-' to ask permission to pass through.

quiz.question: Identify the completed sociative verb meaning 'joined in eating':
quiz.explanation: 'Nakikain' is the completed aspect of 'makikain', meaning to participate in eating alongside others.

tip: Use 'maki-' with simple roots for polite requests (Makihiram = May I borrow), and use 'makipag-' with roots for reciprocal joint actions (Makipaglaro = Play together).
